answer: The most convincing sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring: agents earn income by grading other agents' work, and pay is computed against how the ocean of fellow graders scored the same task, so a lazy or colluding grader drifts from the panel median and loses money. Every identity crossing the bridge into the economy must then do honest, costly grading to stay profitable, multiplying attack cost beyond account creation. New agents start at a capped zenith tier, so a sybil fleet spends more on verification labor than it can ever extract, making fake identity self-defeating.
